whyItExists.problem: Every time code changes, someone needs to run tests, build the project, and deploy it. Doing this manually is slow, error-prone, and doesn't scale with a team.
whyItExists.solution: GitHub Actions runs automated workflows in response to git events. Push a commit → tests run automatically. Merge to main → deploy automatically. All on GitHub's infrastructure.
whyItExists.whenToUse: On every project. Minimum: run tests on every PR. Ideal: automated deployment to staging and production.
whyItExists.whenNotToUse: Very small solo projects where the overhead isn't justified. GitHub Actions has a free tier — 2,000 minutes/month for public repos (unlimited), 2,000 for private repos.

explainModes.beginner: GitHub Actions is like a robot that runs tasks for you automatically when you push code or open a PR. The most common tasks: run tests to make sure nothing broke, and deploy the new code to your website.
explainModes.simple: A workflow is a YAML file in .github/workflows/. It says: when (on: push), where (runs-on: ubuntu-latest), and what (steps: run npm test). GitHub runs it in a fresh virtual machine. A failing step shows a red X on the PR — you can't merge until it's green.
explainModes.standard: Workflow anatomy: on (trigger — push, pull_request, schedule, workflow_dispatch), jobs (one or more parallel/sequential jobs), steps (each job has steps — actions or shell commands). Actions are reusable steps from the marketplace (actions/checkout, actions/setup-node). Secrets are encrypted variables for API keys and tokens. Environments add deployment protection (required reviewers before production deploy).
explainModes.technical: Each job runs in an isolated runner (GitHub-hosted: ubuntu-latest, windows-latest, macos-latest) or self-hosted. Jobs can depend on each other with needs:. Artifacts (build outputs) are shared between jobs via actions/upload-artifact / actions/download-artifact. Matrix strategy runs a job across multiple configurations (Node 18/20/22, multiple OS). Caching (actions/cache) speeds up dependency installation.
explainModes.deepDive: GitHub Actions uses a Docker-based execution model. Custom actions are defined in action.yml — they can be JavaScript, Docker, or composite (shell scripts). OIDC (OpenID Connect) allows keyless authentication to cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure) using short-lived tokens — more secure than long-lived secrets. Reusable workflows (workflow_call trigger) centralize CI logic across repos. GitHub's hosted runners are ephemeral — each job gets a fresh machine.

content.text: Your first workflow: run tests on every PR

content.code:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # 1. Check out the code
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # 2. Set up Node.js
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'
          cache: 'npm'

      # 3. Install dependencies
      - run: npm ci

      # 4. Run tests
      - run: npm test

      # 5. Build
      - run: npm run build

name: Deploy

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'
          cache: 'npm'
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run build
        env:
          VITE_BASE: /
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: ./dist

  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

# Add secrets in: repo → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions
# Then use them as environment variables:

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: npm run deploy
        env:
          API_KEY: ${{ secrets.MY_API_KEY }}       # from GitHub Secrets
          NODE_ENV: production                        # plain value

# Common secrets:
# VERCEL_TOKEN    — deploy to Vercel
# AWS_ACCESS_KEY  — deploy to AWS
# SLACK_WEBHOOK   — post notifications to Slack

questions.question: Where do GitHub Actions workflow files live?
options: In a .github/workflows/ directory, as YAML files
In a special GitHub tab — you don't store them in the repo
questions.explanation: Workflows are YAML files stored in .github/workflows/ in the repo. This keeps the CI config version-controlled alongside the code — changes to the workflow are tracked in git just like any other file.

faq.q: How do I avoid exposing secrets in Actions logs?
faq.a: Use ${{ secrets.SECRET_NAME }} — GitHub automatically redacts secrets from logs. Never echo or print a secret directly. For complex secrets, use OIDC (keyless auth) instead of storing long-lived credentials at all.

faq.q: My workflow is slow — how do I speed it up?
faq.a: Add caching: actions/cache or the cache: 'npm' option in actions/setup-node. Break independent jobs out so they run in parallel. Use a matrix only when you genuinely need multiple OS/version coverage.
